newsitem.title: UK: CME signs clearing, trading link with France's MATIF, SBF.
newsitem.headline: CME signs clearing, trading link with France's MATIF, SBF.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange signed an agreement Thursday with France's MATIF and the SBF-Paris Bourse to link their clearing systems.
Under the deal, CME will swap its Clearing 21 system in return for the SBF-Paris Bourse's NSC electronic trading system, officials said at a signing ceremony in London.
The signing was made to coincide with the International Derivatives Conference in London.
Officials said Clearing 21, which matches and clears futures and options trades, would be expanded for clearing equity securities and cash market instruments.
Similarly, the SBF-Paris Bourse NSC system used for equity securities and equity options would be modified to trade futures and options on futures as well.
Separately, heads of the three exchanges also signed a letter of intent to license and market the entire package of trading and clearing systems to other potential exchanges.
The new system is expected to be implemented in the second half of 1998.
The new system, which was expected to halve trading costs in five years, would serve as the new operating system for GLOBEX, the after-hours electronic system of the CME and Matif.

Asked whether a project for a similar link-up between the CME and the Chicago Board of Trade was moving forward, CME Chairman Jack Sandner said, "We're moving along. We're analysing the hardware now."
